The '''grappling spike launcher''', also known as a '''liquid-cable launcher''', was a device that launched a liquid that immediately solidified into a tough yet lightweight and flexible [[monofilament cable]] upon exposure to most habitable [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheres]].

==Description==
This grappling spike launcher could attach to [[Grappling hook/Legends|grappling hooks]] or be used for swinglines. They were found across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for a price of about fifty [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]], and were often used by [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]], soldiers, [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], explorers and emergency rescue teams. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] also fabricated their own grappling spike launchers in their workshops on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], for use by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] on field operations.

The standard design featured a dual-strand [[Liquid cable|liquid-cable]] reservoir, launching twin cables that wrapped around one another to create a much stronger line. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Jedi such as [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] carried simple fibercord grappling hooks in their utility belts as opposed to liquid-cable launchers.

The grappling spike launcher was a small device commonly carried in a [[Jedi utility belt/Legends|Jedi's utility belt]]. It comprised a central unit containing a liquid-cable reservoir, a grappling hook in one end, and a spike launcher in the other end. The liquid-cable reservoir was large enough to form up to 200 meters of cable. When launched, the spike's liquid-cable would solidify, and would be fired with enough momentum to embed the spike in most surfaces&mdash;excluding materials such as tough metals or [[Particle shield/Legends|particle shielded]] surfaces. The hook could then be attached to a solid object to secure the line.

Grappling spike launchers could be used by themselves or as attachments for blasters and blaster-rifles. When attached to blasters and/or blaster-rifles, this assembly (and sometimes the grappling-spike-launchers themselves) were called [[Ascension gun/Legends|ascension guns]].

==History==
The [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] carried liquid-cable launchers on many missions. [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and Obi-Wan Kenobi were equipped with grappling spike launchers during their mission to [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. When their [[Tribubble bongo/Legends|Gungan bongo]] became caught in the current of the [[Virdugo Plunge/Legends|Virdugo Plunge]] in [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], the Jedi used their grappling spike launchers to escape the doomed craft and reach dry land. Later, during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Second Battle of Theed]], [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]] and [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] used ascension guns that contained these devices to scale the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Theed Royal Palace]]. [[19 BBY/Legends|13 years later]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] would use their fibercord grappling hooks to reach safety in an elevator shaft onboard the damaged [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]].

[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker]] used liquid-cable launchers during their explorations aboard ''[[Outbound Flight]]''. In [[44 ABY]] Luke Skywalker used a cable launcher on [[Pydyr]] in the hunt for [[Abeloth]] to descend to the cave by the sea.<ref name="Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref>
